quests.title: The Sibling's Cache
quests.summary: Three weeks before the strike, the scout's brother buried an emergency crate behind the family house. The quadrant it stood in no longer has street signs.

stages.title: The Cadastral Sheets
stages.description: The map drawer holds three sheets that cover the old residential quadrant. None of them agree with each other.

choices.label: Work the sheets until the grids agree
choices.description: Three maps, two nights, a ruler and a borrowed lamp.
choices.consequence_summary: The route is walkable and the corner is marked in pencil. He sleeps through a full watch for the first time in a week.

choices.label: Go on memory. He grew up on that street.
choices.description: Pack the gear tonight and trust the shape of the place.
choices.consequence_summary: The gear is packed by midnight. He spends the rest of the night listing what he might have misremembered.

stages.title: Under the Basement Stairs
stages.description: The house came down into its own basement. Reaching the crate means shoring the stair wall first, and shoring takes metal.

choices.label: Turn the medicine over to the infirmary
choices.description: Four sealed courses of antibiotics, still in date by the crate's own label.
choices.consequence_summary: The infirmary logs the courses and does not ask where they came from. He keeps the crate lid, which has his brother's handwriting on it.

choices.label: Keep the locket and what was under it
choices.description: The crate held more than medicine, and nobody counted it going in.
choices.consequence_summary: Nobody asks and he does not offer. Some nights he takes the locket out, looks at it, and puts it back in the same pocket.

quests.title: The Last Confession
quests.summary: The shelter's doctor worked a checkpoint triage line in the last month of the war, and sorted officers to the front of it. She has never written down why.

stages.title: Night Shifts, Written Down
stages.description: She writes the checkpoint out longhand on the backs of dosage sheets, three nights running, getting further each night before she stops.

choices.label: Read it out to the council
choices.description: Say it once, in a room, to people who will still be there tomorrow.
choices.consequence_summary: She reads it badly, in a flat voice, and nobody interrupts. The minutes for that evening run to one line.

choices.label: Put the pages in the incinerator
choices.description: Feed them in, wait for the draught, close the hatch.
choices.consequence_summary: The pages go. What was on them does not: she can still recite the third paragraph.

stages.title: The Antiseptic Run
stages.description: She books herself onto every ward shift going and cooks antiseptic wash out of base reagents in the hours between.

choices.label: Post a triage order: worst first, rank ignored
choices.description: Write it on the ward wall at eye height, where the queue can read it.
choices.consequence_summary: It goes up in pencil, signed. Twice since, someone senior has read it, gone to the back of the line, and let that be seen.

choices.label: Work the ward by the numbers and nothing else
choices.description: Sort by survivability, record the outcome, do not learn the names.
choices.consequence_summary: Her hands have stopped shaking and her wash is the cleanest in the shelter. She has also stopped calling patients anything but the bed number.

quests.title: Signals from Sector 4
quests.summary: A carrier wave repeats on emergency channel 14 every ninety minutes. The callsign under it belongs to a civil defense relay that is supposed to be slag.

stages.title: The Copper Choke
stages.description: The signal sits under the noise floor. Pulling it out means winding a tuned choke from salvaged copper and hoping the transistor stage holds.

choices.label: Run the transistor stage past its rating
choices.description: Spend spare diodes to buy a clean recording.
choices.consequence_summary: Two diodes cook. The audio comes up out of the hiss: a beacon, looped, machine-timed, with no voice anywhere in it.

choices.label: Keep it inside tolerance
choices.description: Slower, quieter, and the parts survive the night.
choices.consequence_summary: The recording is noisy and the callsign is unmistakable regardless. Nothing in the rack is damaged, which counts for something.

stages.title: Three Watches of Timestamps
stages.description: The message is in the intervals, not the tone. Logging it takes three watches and a wristwatch nobody else is allowed to borrow.

choices.label: Key a short reply and let it go
choices.description: Eleven seconds of transmission, then off the air.
choices.consequence_summary: Ninety minutes later the loop comes back with an extra chime on the end of it. The comms room talks about nothing else for a week.

choices.label: Log it. Stay dark.
choices.description: Write the frequency down. Do not put the shelter on the air.
choices.consequence_summary: The frequency goes in the book with the date and nothing else. Whoever is transmitting keeps transmitting, and never learns that anyone heard.

quests.title: Pages of the Lost
quests.summary: The archivist is trying to assemble one honest account of the last forty-eight hours before the strike, out of the memories of people who were on the skyway when the sirens went.

stages.title: What They Saw From the Skyway
stages.description: Eleven residents were above ground that morning. Nine will talk about it. Two start, and stop.

choices.label: Let them tell it at their own speed
choices.description: Sit through the silences. Come back tomorrow when the silence wins.
choices.consequence_summary: It takes three weeks instead of one. Two accounts stay unusable, and both of those people come back later, on their own, to finish.

choices.label: Take timings, wind, and shockwave delay only
choices.description: Keep the questions narrow and the pages clean.
choices.consequence_summary: The timings agree to within ninety seconds, which no account of that morning has managed before. Nobody comes back to add anything.

stages.title: Canvas and Glue
stages.description: Ninety-odd pages, no binder's thread, and a glue pot thinned twice to make it stretch.

choices.label: Put it on the library shelf, unlocked
choices.description: Anyone can take it down. Anyone can read what their neighbours said.
choices.consequence_summary: It comes back to the shelf with pencil in the margins. Someone has corrected a street name. Someone else has added a name to the list at the back.

choices.label: File it with the council, sealed
choices.description: Out of the damp, out of the arguments, out of reach.
choices.consequence_summary: The binding will outlast everyone named in it. Two of the eleven have asked to read their own account and been told the request goes to the council.

quests.title: The Smith's Promise
quests.summary: The engineer promised a dying colleague a spring-loaded leg brace for his daughter. The girl is nine, and she has outgrown two of them already.

stages.title: The Drafting Desk
stages.description: Caliper readings taken off the girl's knee twice, a week apart, because she is still growing.

choices.label: Build it heavy: damped struts, load-bearing
choices.description: Assume she will carry things. Assume she will fall.
choices.consequence_summary: The drawing is finished and the strut stock set aside. It will weigh what a full water can weighs, and it will not break.

choices.label: Build it light: thin stock, quick hinge
choices.description: Assume ladderways, narrow doors, and a nine-year-old in a hurry.
choices.consequence_summary: The drawing is finished and the thin stock set aside. It will let her keep up on the stairs, and it will need watching.

stages.title: Tempering the Hinge
stages.description: Two hinges forged, quenched, and drawn back in the maintenance oven until the colour comes right.

choices.label: Fit it properly. Take the extra days.
choices.description: Leather at every contact point, then walk her up and down the corridor until nothing rubs.
choices.consequence_summary: Four more days and one remade cuff. She wears it out of the shop without being told to, and the engineer sits down on the bench afterward and stays there a while.

choices.label: Load-test it in the warehouse first
choices.description: Put it under haulage weight and find the failure before the girl does.
choices.consequence_summary: It survives a shift of loaded crates and comes back scuffed and true. The fitting waits another week, which the girl counts.

quests.title: The Lichen Tincture
quests.summary: The dry cough is through half the lower dormitory. The farmer thinks a lichen off the surface intake housing will make a tincture that helps, and is trying to grow it on purpose.

stages.title: The Sporebed
stages.description: Damp medium in the end drip bed, seeded from a scraping off the intake housing, kept dark.

choices.label: Feed it kitchen trimmings
choices.description: Push the mycelium hard and accept the contamination risk.
choices.consequence_summary: It takes the bed in nine days and smells like wet bread. Two trays have something else growing in them that nobody ordered.

choices.label: Keep it under glass
choices.description: Sealed jars, one opening a day, nothing shared with the food beds.
choices.consequence_summary: Growth is slow enough to be boring and clean enough to bet on. Nothing has crossed into the food rows.

stages.title: The Retort
stages.description: Harvest, mash, and distill in clean water. Glass is the bottleneck: there are two retorts and one of them is cracked.

choices.label: A spoonful a day to anyone coughing
choices.description: Run it out to the dormitories while there is any left.
choices.consequence_summary: The lower dormitory is quieter at night inside a week. The stock is gone in eleven days and the next batch is thirty days out.

choices.label: Reduce it down for the trauma locker
choices.description: Small vials, high strength, held back for the cases that stop breathing.
choices.consequence_summary: Six vials go into the locker under the surgeon's key. The dormitories keep coughing, and the next time somebody comes in blue there will be something on the shelf for them.

quests.title: The Tarnished Locket
quests.summary: The locket holds photographs of two children who did not reach the shelter. The hinge is sprung, and it will not stay shut in a pocket.

stages.title: Fine Wire
stages.description: The hinge pin is thinner than anything in the parts bins. The nearest match is inside a dead instrument panel.

choices.label: Sit with it alone, all night, under the loupe
choices.description: One pin, one alignment, no scratches across the portraits.
choices.consequence_summary: It shuts with a small sound. It gets opened and closed eleven times to be sure, and then stays shut for a week.

choices.label: Ask the engineer to hold the light
choices.description: Two people at one bench, and the story comes out while the pin goes in.
choices.consequence_summary: The pin seats on the second try. Somebody else in the shelter now knows both names, and says them out loud, correctly.

stages.title: One Candle, One Evening
stages.description: A tallow candle lit at the hour the sirens went, on the anniversary that nobody puts on the roster.

choices.label: Put the locket back on and take the nursery watch
choices.description: Turn the keeping of it into the keeping of the children who are here.
choices.consequence_summary: The locket goes back under the collar. The nursery roster has a new name against the small hours, and the name turns up.

choices.label: Close it and lay it in the memorial niche
choices.description: Leave the keepsake in the wall with the others and walk back to the bunks.
choices.consequence_summary: It sits in the niche among ration-tin lids and pressed leaves. The walk back to the bunks is the long part, and it gets done.

quests.title: Blood Debt
quests.summary: A drifter is sitting out on the airlock apron wearing the brigade flash that the veteran spent four years being shot at by.

stages.title: From the Watchtower Slit
stages.description: The drifter stays on the apron for two days: out of throwing range, not signalling, not leaving.

choices.label: Put a question to them over the external speaker
choices.description: Ask what the flash on the sleeve means and make them answer it.
choices.consequence_summary: The answer comes back rehearsed, and then stops being rehearsed. They walked out on the brigade before the exchange, and what they want is water.

choices.label: Stand the watch to and check the seals
choices.description: Treat the flash as reconnaissance until proven otherwise.
choices.consequence_summary: Every seal on the north face is checked twice and holds. The drifter is still out there on the third morning, sitting down now.

stages.title: At the Threshold
stages.description: Four cans of clean water is what the decision costs either way: handed out at the door, or carried back down to the store.

choices.label: Open the outer door. Water first, questions later.
choices.description: Take the risk of the flash on the sleeve for the sake of whoever is under it.
choices.consequence_summary: They drink sitting on the airlock floor with both hands round the can. The veteran stands the whole time and never says what that flash used to mean.

choices.label: Send them off at gunpoint
choices.description: No former enemy comes through this door, whatever they are now.
choices.consequence_summary: They go west along the ridge and are out of sight inside the hour. The seals hold, the shelter is intact, and the veteran keeps checking the ridge for a week.

quests.title: The Corridor Songs
quests.summary: The old music teacher is writing folk tunes down from memory on the backs of ration sheets, because the corridors at night are very quiet and the children have started to notice.

stages.title: Staves on Ration Paper
stages.description: Five-line staves ruled by hand between shifts, and a memory that argues with itself about the third verse.

choices.label: Teach the tunes to the youngest first
choices.description: Afternoons in the mess hall, no instruments, everybody loud.
choices.consequence_summary: By the second week the tunes are audible in the corridors at odd hours, sung wrong, with new words in them.

choices.label: Set it in three parts for the off-shift
choices.description: Adults, evenings, the harmony held down by whoever can hold a line.
choices.consequence_summary: Nine adults turn up, then fourteen. They are not good, and they stay an hour past the lamp-out warning.

stages.title: The Recital
stages.description: One evening, one bulb on the generator's good circuit, and the whole shelter in a room built for half of it.

choices.label: Close with a tune the shelter wrote itself
choices.description: Their own words, in a key that everybody can reach.
choices.consequence_summary: It is sung twice, because after the first time nobody moves. For weeks afterward people hum it on the stairs without noticing they are doing it.

choices.label: Close with something quiet
choices.description: Send them down to the bunks instead of sending them up.
choices.consequence_summary: The room empties slowly, and the corridors stay quiet in a different way than before. The night watch logs the fewest wakings in a month.

quests.title: The Watcher's Blindspot
quests.summary: On a routine walk the sentry finds a maintenance shaft eaten thin by rust. It comes in behind the airlock barricades entirely.

stages.title: Measuring the Rust
stages.description: A crawl the length of the sub-ventilation run with a lamp in the teeth, tapping for wall thickness.

choices.label: Recommend welding it closed
choices.description: Trade the secondary air circulation for a wall nobody can get through.
choices.consequence_summary: The shaft becomes wall. Air in the lower dormitory goes stale by the end of every second shift, and everybody knows exactly why.

choices.label: Keep the airflow. Wire it instead.
choices.description: Silent trips at two points, checked on the round.
choices.consequence_summary: Air keeps moving and the trips are set. The plan now depends on somebody walking the round, every round, indefinitely.

stages.title: The Grate
stages.description: Grate plate bolted across the shaft mouth, backed with surplus rebar cut to length.

choices.label: Put your own name against the night inspection
choices.description: Walk the ducting at the top of every graveyard shift, personally.
choices.consequence_summary: The grate holds and the walk gets done. It is a promise with no end date on it, made by one person, and the roster has started planning around it.

choices.label: Set spring-loaded traps in the shaft
choices.description: Let the shaft do the work and stop sending a person into it.
choices.consequence_summary: Nobody has to crawl the run at night any more. Whatever comes down it will not be asked who it is first, and the maintenance crew has stopped using the shortcut.
